analysis:
Examined SSDWholeRootMaintainer.swift (head), plus two test files (SSDCheckpointFileCoordinatorTests, SSDCheckpointMaintenanceEpochTests). Relevant threat: T-041 (encrypted SSD prefix cache, 30-min sliding TTL, disk-budget LRU, accepted SEC-035).

Changed behavior: the TTL sweep (SSDWholeRootMaintainer.swift lines 148-166) now passes unusedSince: nowSeconds - ttlSeconds to SSDDiskBudget.shared.retireActiveEntries, so a loaded store can keep a file whose index saw a hit after the cutoff (the mtime from the scan can trail the hit). Survivors have their mtime re-read (lines 161-165) so budget eviction orders by the fresh mtime. OwnedFile.modifiedAt became var (line 27). Security effect: TTL enforcement is now sliding on the in-memory last hit and is bounded by the cutoff, which is consistent with the documented sliding TTL. The retention extension is limited to entries actually hit within the TTL window, so it does not extend the documented 30-minute bound. The unloaded-model fallback path (SSDCacheEpochStore.performUnloadedDestructiveChange) is unchanged and still deletes by mtime. Budget eviction (lines 171-197) calls removeOwned without unusedSince, so budget enforcement is unaffected by the new guard. The sweep's header-readability ownership proof, the lstat identity cache, safe-root checks and symlink rejection are unchanged in the diff.

Tests: the coordinator tests exercise shared/exclusive modes, upgrade/downgrade and cancellation; they are test-only and add no attack surface. The epoch test now touches the index so the victim is genuinely idle.

Remaining uncertainty: the implementation of SSDDiskBudget.retireActiveEntries(unusedSince:) and of SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator's shared/exclusive mode (and any upgrade/downgrade paths) is outside the supplied evidence. The next pass should confirm that a retired-but-hit entry is not retained beyond the TTL when the index has a stale touch, and that the coordinator's reader/writer semantics match what the tests assert.
